rancher-cluster-1.2: CPU busy percentage for all reported nodes, calculated as one minus idle CPU time and averaged across cores. 100% means all measured CPU time is non-idle. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-1.3: Linux load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes for all reported nodes: tasks running, ready to run, or waiting uninterruptibly, often for disk I/O. These are task counts, not percentages. Compare load with the number of CPU cores; sustained load above that count suggests contention. Windows series show average processor queue length over the same windows.
rancher-cluster-1.4: Percentage of physical RAM unavailable for new work for all reported nodes, calculated as total minus available memory divided by total. Includes host processes and is not a measure of pod requests or limits.
rancher-cluster-1.5: Used filesystem capacity for all reported nodes, weighted by filesystem size. Calculated from total minus free bytes; this measures storage occupancy, not disk activity. Rootfs aliases and certain Windows virtual volumes are excluded.
rancher-cluster-1.6: Disk read and write throughput in bytes per second for all reported nodes, summed across reported disks. High throughput alone does not show whether a disk is saturated; compare latency and utilization. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-1.7: Network packet, dropped-packet and error rates per second for all reported nodes, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Persistent drops or errors warrant investigation. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-1.8: Linux network bytes received and transmitted per second for all reported nodes, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Throughput is not a measure of packet loss. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.

rancher-cluster-nodes-1.2: CPU busy percentage for each reported node, calculated as one minus idle CPU time and averaged across cores. 100% means all measured CPU time is non-idle. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.3: Linux load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes for each reported node: tasks running, ready to run, or waiting uninterruptibly, often for disk I/O. These are task counts, not percentages. Compare load with the number of CPU cores; sustained load above that count suggests contention. Windows series show average processor queue length over the same windows.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.4: Percentage of physical RAM unavailable for new work for each reported node, calculated as total minus available memory divided by total. Includes host processes and is not a measure of pod requests or limits.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.5: Used filesystem capacity for each reported node, weighted by filesystem size. Calculated from total minus free bytes; this measures storage occupancy, not disk activity. Rootfs aliases and certain Windows virtual volumes are excluded.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.6: Disk read and write throughput in bytes per second for each reported node, summed across reported disks. High throughput alone does not show whether a disk is saturated; compare latency and utilization. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.7: Network packet, dropped-packet and error rates per second for each reported node, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Persistent drops or errors warrant investigation. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-cluster-nodes-1.8: Linux network bytes received and transmitted per second for each reported node, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Throughput is not a measure of packet loss. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.

rancher-etcd-1.2: etcd client gRPC bytes received and sent per second, summed across etcd members. This measures communication with clients, not replication traffic between members. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-1.3: Allocated etcd database size in bytes, summed across etcd members. Includes unused space inside the database file; it is not just the size of live keys. Sustained growth should be compared with the database quota.
rancher-etcd-1.4: Currently open Watch and Lease bidirectional gRPC streams, summed across etcd members, estimated as streams started minus streams completed. Long-lived streams are normal and do not represent queued requests.
rancher-etcd-1.5: Raft proposals committed, applied and failed per second, summed across etcd members. Pending is a current count of proposals awaiting commit, not a per-second rate. Sustained pending growth or failures can indicate an unhealthy or overloaded etcd cluster. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-1.6: Unary gRPC calls started and calls completed with a non-OK status per second, summed across etcd members. The error series is a count per second, not an error percentage. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-1.7: Estimated p99 disk latency for write-ahead-log fsync and backend commits, in seconds, separately for each etcd member. About 99% of observed operations completed within this duration. Higher values can slow control-plane writes. An empty interval means there were no usable histogram observations. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.

rancher-etcd-nodes-1.2: etcd client gRPC bytes received and sent per second, for each etcd member. This measures communication with clients, not replication traffic between members. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-nodes-1.3: Allocated etcd database size in bytes, for each etcd member. Includes unused space inside the database file; it is not just the size of live keys. Sustained growth should be compared with the database quota.
rancher-etcd-nodes-1.4: Currently open Watch and Lease bidirectional gRPC streams, for each etcd member, estimated as streams started minus streams completed. Long-lived streams are normal and do not represent queued requests.
rancher-etcd-nodes-1.5: Raft proposals committed, applied and failed per second, for each etcd member. Pending is a current count of proposals awaiting commit, not a per-second rate. Sustained pending growth or failures can indicate an unhealthy or overloaded etcd cluster. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-nodes-1.6: Unary gRPC calls started and calls completed with a non-OK status per second, for each etcd member. The error series is a count per second, not an error percentage. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-etcd-nodes-1.7: Estimated p99 disk latency for write-ahead-log fsync and backend commits, in seconds, separately for each etcd member. About 99% of observed operations completed within this duration. Higher values can slow control-plane writes. An empty interval means there were no usable histogram observations. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.

rancher-k8s-components-1.2: Kubernetes API requests per second, summed across API servers and grouped by HTTP status. 4xx responses usually indicate rejected client requests; 5xx responses indicate server-side failures. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-k8s-components-1.3: Current number of work items waiting in each listed controller queue, summed across server instances. Brief spikes are expected during changes; sustained growth means controllers are falling behind. A missing controller series is not the same as an empty queue.
rancher-k8s-components-1.4: Current number of pods whose Scheduled condition is false, across the cluster. These pods have not yet been assigned to a node. A sustained nonzero value warrants checking resource availability, placement constraints and pod events.
rancher-k8s-components-1.5: NGINX ingress connections: reading, waiting and writing are current connection counts; accepted and handled count newly accepted or handled connections during each rolling Grafana rate interval. These are different measurements, not five equivalent rates. This panel requires NGINX ingress metrics; a cluster using only Traefik will have no data.

rancher-k8s-components-nodes-1.2: Kubernetes API requests per second, separately by API-server instance and HTTP status. 4xx responses usually indicate rejected client requests; 5xx responses indicate server-side failures. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-k8s-components-nodes-1.3: Current number of work items waiting in each listed controller queue for each server instance. Brief spikes are expected during changes; sustained growth means controllers are falling behind. A missing controller series is not the same as an empty queue.
rancher-k8s-components-nodes-1.4: Current number of pods whose Scheduled condition is false, across the cluster. These pods have not yet been assigned to a node. A sustained nonzero value warrants checking resource availability, placement constraints and pod events.
rancher-k8s-components-nodes-1.5: NGINX ingress connections: reading, waiting and writing are current connection counts; accepted and handled count newly accepted or handled connections during each rolling Grafana rate interval. These are different measurements, not five equivalent rates. This panel requires NGINX ingress metrics; a cluster using only Traefik will have no data.

rancher-node-1.2: CPU busy percentage for the selected node, calculated as one minus idle CPU time and averaged across cores. 100% means all measured CPU time is non-idle. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-1.3: Linux load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes for the selected node: tasks running, ready to run, or waiting uninterruptibly, often for disk I/O. These are task counts, not percentages. Compare load with the number of CPU cores; sustained load above that count suggests contention. Windows series show average processor queue length over the same windows.
rancher-node-1.4: Percentage of physical RAM unavailable for new work for the selected node, calculated as total minus available memory divided by total. Includes host processes and is not a measure of pod requests or limits.
rancher-node-1.5: Used filesystem capacity for the selected node, weighted by filesystem size. Calculated from total minus free bytes; this measures storage occupancy, not disk activity. Rootfs aliases and certain Windows virtual volumes are excluded.
rancher-node-1.6: Disk read and write throughput in bytes per second for the selected node, summed across reported disks. High throughput alone does not show whether a disk is saturated; compare latency and utilization. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-1.7: Network packet, dropped-packet and error rates per second for the selected node, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Persistent drops or errors warrant investigation. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-1.8: Linux network bytes received and transmitted per second for the selected node, summed across selected interfaces. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Throughput is not a measure of packet loss. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-1.1001: CPU core and package/control sensor temperatures in degrees Celsius on the selected node, at each sample. AMD systems may expose only shared CPU sensors. VPS hosts usually expose no hardware sensors: missing data does not mean 0 degrees. GPU and disk sensors are excluded. Compare sustained temperatures with the CPU manufacturer's limits.

rancher-node-detail-1.2: CPU time by mode for the selected node, averaged across CPU cores. Idle is spare CPU capacity; user and system represent application and kernel work. All modes together account for total CPU time. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-detail-1.3: Linux load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes for the selected node: tasks running, ready to run, or waiting uninterruptibly, often for disk I/O. These are task counts, not percentages. Compare load with the number of CPU cores; sustained load above that count suggests contention. Windows series show average processor queue length over the same windows.
rancher-node-detail-1.4: Percentage of physical RAM unavailable for new work for the selected node, calculated as total minus available memory divided by total. Includes host processes and is not a measure of pod requests or limits.
rancher-node-detail-1.5: Used filesystem capacity for the selected node, separately by device. Calculated from total minus free bytes; this measures storage occupancy, not disk activity. Rootfs aliases and certain Windows virtual volumes are excluded.
rancher-node-detail-1.6: Disk read and write throughput in bytes per second for the selected node, separately by device. High throughput alone does not show whether a disk is saturated; compare latency and utilization. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-detail-1.7: Network packet, dropped-packet and error rates per second for the selected node, separately by interface. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Persistent drops or errors warrant investigation. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-detail-1.8: Linux network bytes received and transmitted per second for the selected node, separately by interface. Loopback and common container/overlay interfaces are excluded. Throughput is not a measure of packet loss. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-node-detail-1.1001: CPU core and package/control sensor temperatures in degrees Celsius on the selected node, at each sample. AMD systems may expose only shared CPU sensors. VPS hosts usually expose no hardware sensors: missing data does not mean 0 degrees. GPU and disk sensors are excluded. Compare sustained temperatures with the CPU manufacturer's limits.

rancher-pod-1.2: CPU usage for the selected pod, expressed as equivalent CPU cores. Total includes user and system time, so do not add those series together. Throttled is CPU time withheld by quota enforcement per second; sustained throttling can slow requests even when the host has spare CPU. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-pod-1.4: Current memory for the selected pod, in bytes: Linux working set or Windows committed memory. Working set excludes reclaimable inactive file cache. This is usage, not a percentage of a configured limit.
rancher-pod-1.7: Packets received and sent, dropped packets and network errors per second for the selected pod. Persistent drops or errors can indicate congestion or network problems; packet volume alone is not bandwidth. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-pod-1.8: Network bytes received and sent per second for the selected pod. Compare the two directions separately; this measures throughput rather than connection count. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-pod-1.6: Filesystem bytes read and written per second for the selected pod. This measures throughput, not disk space used or operation latency. Some runtimes do not expose filesystem counters for every container. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.

rancher-pod-containers-1.2: CPU usage for each container in the selected pod, expressed as equivalent CPU cores. Total includes user and system time, so do not add those series together. Throttled is CPU time withheld by quota enforcement per second; sustained throttling can slow requests even when the host has spare CPU. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
rancher-pod-containers-1.4: Current memory for each container in the selected pod, in bytes: Linux working set or Windows committed memory. Working set excludes reclaimable inactive file cache. This is usage, not a percentage of a configured limit.
rancher-pod-containers-1.7: Packets received and sent, dropped packets and network errors per second for each container in the selected pod. Persistent drops or errors can indicate congestion or network problems; packet volume alone is not bandwidth. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range. Containers share the pod network namespace, so network counters may be attributed only to the pod sandbox rather than every application container.
rancher-pod-containers-1.8: Network bytes received and sent per second for each container in the selected pod. Compare the two directions separately; this measures throughput rather than connection count. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range. Containers share the pod network namespace, so network counters may be attributed only to the pod sandbox rather than every application container.
rancher-pod-containers-1.6: Filesystem bytes read and written per second for each container in the selected pod. This measures throughput, not disk space used or operation latency. Some runtimes do not expose filesystem counters for every container. Rates use the rolling interval chosen by Grafana for the selected time range; they are not totals over that range.
